# zgehrd

> Reduces a complex general matrix to upper Hessenberg form using a blocked algorithm.

<section class="intro">

When `WORK` is `null`, this wrapper allocates the optimal workspace of `N*NB + TSIZE` (with `TSIZE = 4160`)
complex elements as a convenience. Prefer passing a caller-owned buffer for batched use.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgehrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgehrd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgehrd( order, N, ilo, ihi, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | Lower index of the balanced matrix (1-based)<br>Rejects `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max(1, N)` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | Upper index of the balanced matrix (1-based)<br>Rejects `ihi < min(ilo, N) \|\| ihi > N` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **out** · Output array of scalar factors (length `N-1`) |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | `TAU` stride length (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace, or `null` to allocate the optimum; length at least `max( 1, N )`. For optimum performance it should hold `N*NB + TSIZE` elements (TSIZE = 4160), which enables the blocked path |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ihi`: It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to ZGEBAL; otherwise they should be set to 1 and N respectively. See Further Details. $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`, if $N=0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the upper triangle and the first subdiagonal of A are overwritten with the upper Hessenberg matrix H, and the elements below the first subdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors. See Further Details.
- `TAU`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors (see Further Details). Elements 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`:N-1 of `TAU` are set to zero.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgehrd.ndarray(
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Reduces a complex general matrix to upper Hessenberg form using blocked algorithm.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | Lower index of the balanced matrix<br>Rejects `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max(1, N)` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | Upper index of the balanced matrix<br>Rejects `ihi < min(ilo, N) \|\| ihi > N` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | First stride of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Second stride of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset into A |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **out** · Output array of scalar factors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride of TAU |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset into TAU |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace array; length at least `max( 1, N )`. For optimum performance it should hold `N*NB + TSIZE` elements (TSIZE = 4160), which enables the blocked path |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride of WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset into WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ihi`: It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to ZGEBAL; otherwise they should be set to 1 and N respectively. See Further Details. $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`, if $N=0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the upper triangle and the first subdiagonal of A are overwritten with the upper Hessenberg matrix H, and the elements below the first subdiagonal, with the array `TAU`, represent the unitary matrix Q as a product of elementary reflectors. See Further Details.
- `TAU`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors (see Further Details). Elements 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`:N-1 of `TAU` are set to zero.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info value

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zgehrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgehrd';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
let A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const TAU = new Complex128Array( N - 1 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = zgehrd( 'column-major', N, 1, N, A, N, TAU, 1, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
out = zgehrd.ndarray( N, 1, N, A, 1, N, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGEHRD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGEHRD reduces a complex general matrix A to upper Hessenberg form H by an unitary similarity transformation: $Q^H \, A \, Q = H$ .

### Further Details

The matrix Q is represented as a product of (ihi-ilo) elementary reflectors

Q = H(ilo) H(ilo+1) . . . H(ihi-1).

Each H(i) has the form

$$
H(i) = I - \tau \, v \, v^H
$$

where $\tau$ is a complex scalar, and v is a complex vector with $v(1:i) = 0$, $v(i+1) = 1$ and v(ihi+1:n) = 0; v(i+2:ihi) is stored on exit in `A(i+2:ihi,i)`, and $\tau$ in `TAU(i)`.

The contents of A are illustrated by the following example, with $n = 7$, ilo = 2 and ihi = 6:

```text
on entry,                        on exit,
```

$$
\begin{pmatrix} a & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  & a & a & a & a & a & a \\  &  &  &  &  &  & a \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} a & a & h & h & h & h & a \\  & a & h & h & h & h & a \\  & h & h & h & h & h & h \\  & v_{2} & h & h & h & h & h \\  & v_{2} & v_{3} & h & h & h & h \\  & v_{2} & v_{3} & v_{4} & h & h & h \\  &  &  &  &  &  & a \end{pmatrix}
$$

where a denotes an element of the original matrix A, h denotes a modified element of the upper Hessenberg matrix H, and vi denotes an element of the vector defining H(i).

This file is a slight modification of LAPACK-3.0's ZGEHRD subroutine incorporating improvements proposed by Quintana-Orti and Van de Geijn (2006). (See ZLAHR2.)

</section>
